p.seg: 1.0. Only when the king establishes the state,
does he distinguish the regions and rectify the positions,
embody the state and manage the fields,
in order to provide the people with a standard.
Therefore, he establishes the Tiānguān Zhǒngzǎi,
to lead his subordinates and manage the administration of the state,
in order to assist the king in equally governing the state.
The officials under his administration are:
one hundred and twenty Tú (Foot Soldiers).
*Là rén* (腊人, makers of dried meat),
clerks of the storehouse, two people;
clerks of the storehouse, two people;

1.1. The duties of the Grand Administrator
are to manage the six canons of state building,
in order to assist the king in governing the state:
The first is the Canon of Governance,
and to record the myriad people;
The second is the Canon of Education,
and to guide the myriad people;
The third is the Canon of Rites,
and to harmonize the myriad people;
The fourth is the Canon of Administration,
and to equalize the myriad people;
The fifth is the Canon of Punishments,
and to correct the myriad people;
The sixth is the Canon of Works,
Using the Eight Methods to govern the officialdom:
First is "Guān Shǔ" (官屬, official subordinates),
second is "Guān Zhí" (官職, official duties),
used to differentiate the state's governance;
third is "Guān Lián" (官䏈, official connections),
fourth is "Guān Cháng" (官常, official norms),
fifth is "Guān Chéng" (官成, official achievements),
sixth is "Guān Fǎ" (官法, official laws),
used to rectify the state's governance;
seventh is "Guān Xíng" (官刑, official punishments),
used to correct the state's governance;
eighth is "Guān Jì" (官計, official accounting),
used to manage the state's affairs.
Using the Eight Rules to govern the cities and countryside:
With these eight handles, instruct the king to manage the assembled ministers:
With these eight governing principles, instruct the king to manage the myriad people:
First is to cherish relatives (qīn qīn),
Second is to respect the old (jìng gù),
Third is to advance the worthy (jìn xián),
fifth is "ensuring employment for the mediocre" (bǎo yōng);
eighth is "treating guests with courtesy" (lǐ bīn).
These nine offices are used to assign tasks to the myriad people:
First are the "three agricultural officers" (sān nóng),
third are the "forest and marsh managers" (yú héng),
who produce materials from the mountains and marshes;
who raise and breed birds and beasts;
who fashion and refine the eight materials;
who enrich the flow of goods and commodities;
who process and manage silk and hemp;
who gather and sort raw materials;
but shift around and undertake tasks.
These nine kinds of taxes are used to collect wealth and commodities:
First is the tax from the inner regions of the state (bāng zhōng zhī fù);
second is the tax from the four suburban areas (sì jiāo zhī fù);
Third are the taxes of the *bāng diàn*,
fourth are the taxes of the *jiā xuē*,
fifth are the taxes of the *bāng xiàn*,
sixth are the taxes of the *bāng dū*,
seventh are the taxes of the passes and markets,
eighth are the taxes of the mountains and marshes,
ninth are the taxes of the surplus goods.
Use nine regulations to equally manage finances and resources:
third are regulations for funerals and famines,
fourth are regulations for offerings of food and clothing,
fifth are regulations for construction projects,
sixth are regulations for gifts of currency and silk,
eighth are regulations for extraordinary distributions,
ninth are regulations for generous expenditures.
Use nine kinds of tribute to provide for the needs of the state:
first is tribute for sacrifices (*sì gòng*),
second is tribute for the ladies of the court (*pín gòng*),
third is tribute of vessels (*qì gòng*),
fourth is tribute of currency (*bì gòng*),
fifth is tribute of materials (*cái gòng*),
sixth is tribute of goods (*huò gòng*),
seventh is tribute of clothing (*fú gòng*),
eighth is tribute of banners (*yóu gòng*),
ninth is tribute of miscellaneous items (*wù gòng*).

who gains the people through land;
who gains the people through nobility;
who gains the people through virtue;
who gains the people through the Dao;
who gains the people through clan;
who gains the people through profit;
who gains the people through governance;
who gains the people through trust;
who gains the people through wealth.

He uses the Six Departments of government offices to conduct state administration:
First is the Tiānguān (天官, Officer of Heaven),
in charge of governing the state.
In major matters, they follow their superiors;
in minor matters, they have sole discretion in reporting.
Second is the Dìguān (地官, Officer of Earth),
in charge of the state's education.
In major matters, they follow their superiors;
in minor matters, they have sole discretion in reporting.
Third is the Chūnguān (春官, Officer of Spring),

In major matters, they follow their superiors;
in minor matters, they have sole discretion in reporting.

in charge of the state's administration.

Fifth is the Qiūguān (秋官, Officer of Autumn),

Sixth is the Dōngguān (冬官, Officer of Winter),
in charge of the state's affairs.
In important matters, follow the elders;
Use the six offices of the government to distinguish the governance of the state:
first is the office of governance (zhì zhí),
second is the office of education (jiào zhí),
to bring peace to the myriad people,
third is the office of rites (lǐ zhí),
to bring accord to the myriad people,
fourth is the office of administration (zhèng zhí),
and to gather the hundred kinds of goods;
fifth is the office of punishments (xíng zhí),
sixth is the office of works (shì zhí),
and to produce the hundred kinds of goods.
Use the six alliances (lián) of the government to unite the governance of the state:
First are matters related to sacrifices;
second are matters related to guests;
third are matters related to funerals and famines;
fourth are matters related to military expeditions;
fifth are matters related to agricultural labor;
sixth are matters related to taxation and exemptions.
All minor matters have their associations.
He governed the state using eight achievements of the government:
first, he listened to political affairs and labor services according to the grouping of residences;
second, he listened to the military fields for inspection and verification;
third, he listened to neighborhoods and villages by map;
fourth, he listened to assessments of responsibility according to documents of assignment;
fifth, he listened to emoluments and positions by rituals and commands;
sixth, he listened to receiving and giving by written contracts;
seventh, he listened to buying and selling by quality agreements;
eighth, he listened to entry and exit through established meetings.
By listening to the six accounts of the government offices,
he rectified the administration of the multitude of officials.
